terms.simple: The abdomen is the back section of an insect's body.
terms.more: In the lab it covers segments A1 to A10. Insects usually have no legs here, and the last few segments form the tail end.

terms.simple: An antenna is a feeler on an insect's head that senses smells and touch.
terms.more: Insects have a pair. Antennae are what the front head segment grows when no Hox gene is active there.

terms.simple: An appendage is a body part that sticks out from a segment, like a leg, antenna or wing.
terms.more: Hox genes help decide which appendage each segment grows.

terms.simple: A chromosome is a long strand of DNA that carries many genes.
terms.more: Hox genes sit close together on chromosomes, in roughly the same order as the body parts they control.

terms.simple: Colinearity means Hox genes sit in a row in the same order as the body parts they build.
terms.more: The first gene in the row works near the head, and the last gene works near the tail end.

terms.simple: DNA is the long molecule inside cells that stores the instructions for building a body.
terms.more: Genes are short stretches of DNA.

terms.simple: An elytron is a hard wing cover on a beetle. The plural is elytra.
terms.more: Beetles grow elytra on T2 and fold their flying wings under them.

terms.simple: Evidence is proof from experiments that shows whether an idea is true.
terms.more: The lab labels each change as Documented, Model extrapolation, or Published result differs, so you can see how strong the evidence is.

terms.simple: A gene is a piece of DNA that holds one instruction for the body.
terms.more: Many genes hold the recipe for a protein, and proteins do much of the work in cells.

terms.simple: A haltere is a tiny knob behind a fly's wings that helps it balance in flight.
terms.more: Flies have halteres where other insects have a second pair of wings. They grow on T3.

terms.simple: The head is the front section of an insect's body. It holds the eyes, antennae and mouthparts.
terms.more: In the lab the head has five editable segments: An, Ic, Mn, Mx and Lb.

terms.simple: A Hox gene is a master gene that tells a body segment what to become.
terms.more: Insects in this lab have eight Hox genes: lab, pb, Dfd, Scr, Antp, Ubx, abd-A and Abd-B. They make proteins that switch other genes on or off.

terms.simple: A segment's identity is the instruction that says what it will grow.
terms.more: For example, T2 identity means a midleg and a wing. Hox genes set identity.

terms.simple: A knockout means switching a gene off to see what it does.
terms.more: Scientists compare the changed animal with a normal one to learn the gene's job. It is also called loss of function.

terms.simple: A leg is a jointed limb that an insect walks with. Insects have six.
terms.more: They grow on the three thorax segments T1, T2 and T3, which give the foreleg, midleg and hindleg.

terms.simple: A model is a simple copy of something real that helps us make predictions.
terms.more: The lab's model uses simple rules for how Hox genes set identity. It is useful but leaves out many real details.

terms.simple: Mouthparts are the small parts around an insect's mouth that it uses to bite, chew or lick.
terms.more: They grow on head segments. Examples are the mandible (jaw), the maxilla and palps (feelers), and the labium (lower lip).

terms.simple: A mutant is an animal with a change in one of its genes.
terms.more: Mutants can look different from normal animals, like a fly with four wings. Scientists study them to learn what genes do.

terms.simple: Posterior means toward the back, or the tail end.
terms.more: The opposite is anterior, which means toward the front. The back gene usually wins in the lab's rules.

terms.simple: A protein is a tiny machine made by a cell, following the instructions in a gene.
terms.more: Hox proteins grab onto DNA and switch other genes on or off.

terms.simple: A segment is one repeating piece in the row that makes up an insect's body.
terms.more: The lab has 18 editable segments: An, Ic, Mn, Mx, Lb, T1 to T3 and A1 to A10.

terms.simple: The thorax is the middle section of an insect's body. Legs and wings grow from it.
terms.more: It has three segments, T1, T2 and T3. T1 has a pair of legs. T2 and T3 each have legs and, in most insects, wings.

terms.simple: A wing is a flat flap on an insect's body that it can use to fly.
terms.more: In the lab, wings grow on T2 and T3. Flies change the T3 wing into a haltere, and beetles change the T2 wing into an elytron.
